case_name: Dewan Singh v Champat Singh and others
facts: The appeal by special leave arises from an arbitration proceeding.
The arbitrators made their award on October 11, 1955, and served notice of making and signing the award on the parties to the arbitration agreement.
The appellant filed a suit in the Court of Munsiff Hawaii Meerut praying that the award be made a rule of the court and decree passed in accordance with the same.
The defendants challenged the validity of the award on various grounds, including misconduct by the arbitrators and undue influence.
The Trial Court accepted the contention of the defendants that the arbitrators were guilty of misconduct.
The appellate Court reversed the decree of the Trial Court, holding that the arbitrators had used their personal knowledge in deciding the disputes referred to them.
issues: Whether the arbitrators' decision was vitiated by misconduct
Whether the arbitration agreement empowered the arbitrators to decide the disputes on the basis of their personal knowledge
petitioner_arguments: The arbitrators were not guilty of misconduct
The arbitration agreement did empower the arbitrators to decide the disputes on the basis of their personal knowledge
respondent_arguments: The arbitrators were guilty of misconduct
The arbitration agreement did not empower the arbitrators to decide the disputes on the basis of their personal knowledge
court_reasoning: The arbitrators' decision was vitiated by misconduct because they decided the disputes referred to them primarily on the basis of their personal knowledge.
The arbitration agreement did not specifically empower the arbitrators to decide the disputes on the basis of their personal knowledge.
holding: The appeal fails and is dismissed with costs
The decision reached by the High Court is an eminently just one
cases_cited: the dispute in accordance with the ordinary law-see Chandris v. Isbrandtsen Moller Co
